Subject: Monthly commit proposal & step-up schedule for LaunchPad Games - hosted API usage discounts

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a proposed monthly commit schedule + per-token discount ladder tailored for LaunchPad's flagship mobile launch. High-level summary below and the full spreadsheet is attached (Redwood_Monthly_Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx).

Proposal (monthly committed tokens, hosted API, per-token unit):
- Month 1 (pre-launch month): 50M tokens committed @ $0.0009/token (no discount beyond baseline access)
- Month 2 (launch): 200M tokens committed @ $0.00075/token (10% effective discount vs baseline)
- Month 3: 350M tokens committed @ $0.00068/token (12.5% effective)
- Month 4+: step-up to 500M tokens committed @ $0.0006/token (15% discount) with a 3-month cadence for reviews/adjustments

We built the schedule with a step-up (staircase) approach to accommodate seasonality and a sharp launch spike. Key commercial terms we suggest: 12-month price lock on committed tiers, monthly billing with true-ups if usage exceeds commit, and rollover credits for unused committed tokens up to a 60-day window.

Open items we wanted your feedback on:
- Can procurement sign to monthly billing + monthly true-up?
- Does your finance team need Net 30 vs Net 45 payment terms?
- Would LaunchPad prefer a frontloaded credit (larger Month 1 credit) or a strict staircase as above?

I've also attached the SOW draft (SOW_LaunchPad_v3.docx) and our pricing tiers PDF for reference. If this looks directionally right, we can prepare a redline and hand off to legal/procurement.

Best,
Marcus

We should also understand the true-up mechanics in practice: if we exceed commit by 20% in a month, do we pay overage prorated at list-price or at the discount tier applied retroactively?

Olivia — great questions. Quick answers and then a slightly revised commercial note.

1) Burst capacity & spikes: Redwood Dedicated routing + autoscaling supports short-duration spikes; for hosted API we recommend configuring a burst multiplier and prefix caching to keep tail latency low. We can commit to a soft SLA for burst windows (we'll include a fallback policy). For hard operational needs we can enable reserved burst capacity in the Dedicated pool during the launch week for an incremental fee; details in the SOW.

2) Estimated monthly spend (approx USD):
- Month 1: 50M tokens x $0.0009 = $45,000
- Month 2: 200M tokens x $0.00075 = $150,000
- Month 3: 350M tokens x $0.00068 = $238,000
- Month 4+: 500M tokens x $0.0006 = $300,000/month
(These are committed spend figures; overages would be billed per actuals — see 4) below.)

3) Payment terms & price lock: We can accept PO + Net 45. Price lock will be for committed tiers and will exclude broad model architecture changes that materially change per-token cost (e.g., moving from 7B to 70B if you ask us to swap models). Minor model upgrades and quantization tweaks for perf optimizations will not trigger a price change. We'll put this in the contract language.

4) True-ups and overage mechanics: our standard is to bill overages at the effective discount tier the customer achieved that month — so if your commit + actual usage crosses a higher tier, we'd apply that tier retroactively for the month (this avoids punitive list-priced overages). For example, if you commit 200M but use 250M and cross into the 350M tier, month usage is priced using the 350M effective per-token rate for the whole month's usage. If you'd prefer pay-as-you-go overage at list price instead, we can add that as an option (but customers usually prefer the retroactive tier approach).

I've attached an updated SOW and pricing PDF. If that works, I'll prepare a redline and loop legal/procurement. Neha/Evelyn are on copy to propose a couple alternative step-up schedules below in case you want a frontloaded credit vs a steady staircase.

- Marcus

Marcus Lin

Olivia — adding a couple alternative commit cadence options as requested. Pasted here so procurement/FP&A can see the tradeoffs quickly. Detailed numbers are in the attached XLSX.

Option A — Steady staircase (low ops complexity):
- M1: 50M (pre-launch) — $45k
- M2: 200M — $150k
- M3: 350M — $238k
- M4+: 500M — $300k/mo
Pros: predictable monthly bills; easy true-up math.

Option B — Frontloaded credit (helps cash flow during launch):
- M1: 150M credit applied (prepaid) — equivalent to $120k credit applied against usage in months 1–2
- M2: 250M committed — $187.5k
- M3+: 400M committed — $240k
Pros: Launch month is covered; reduces risk of overage during first spikes. Cons: higher upfront invoice.

Option C — Seasonal buffer (best for unpredictable spikes):
- Baseline commit 300M/mo, with an additional 200M buffer token pool that can be drawn contra a per-draw fee if used; buffer renews monthly or is chargeable on drawdown.
Pros: reduces contract churn; operationally flexible for sudden spikes.

Billing cadence and true-ups: monthly invoices with automated true-up reconciliation. We can include a one-time launch-week reserved capacity charge for guaranteed burst if you want hard guarantees.

Next steps we recommend: (1) pick Option A/B/C or ask us to create a hybrid; (2) Rio legal sends a single redline SOW & commercial terms; (3) Redwood issues the initial invoice/credit if you choose frontload.

-Neha
